drhp.business: The Company operates in only one segment, the real estate business, and holds land and buildings as stock-in-trade for property development. Its revenue arises from rentals of the Company's properties invoiced as fixed monthly charges or on a time-proportionate basis, from real-estate contract cancellations in the usual course of the real estate business, and from interest and dividend income. Its subsidiary, S V Global Finance Private Limited, operates as a non-deposit-taking NBFC.
drhp.end_markets: Indian commercial and residential real estate|Chennai, Tamil Nadu|Bengaluru, Karnataka
drhp.expansion: The annual report discloses no named capex project, no commissioning timeline and no rupee capex quantum. risks.note: The MD&A states that an economic slowdown or recession in a specific industry such as IT/ITES can decrease sales or market rates for residential projects, and that in an extreme downturn the Company may face customer insolvency; a real estate company's business in India is dependent on the easy availability of finance, and a slowdown can cause fund shortages as lenders act safe.
risks.risk: Economic and cyclical exposure of a single real-estate business

risks.note: Management notes the time required to liquidate a real estate property varies with the size, volume, demand, quality and location of the project — the Company's value sits in land inventory that cannot be turned into cash quickly.
risks.risk: Liquidity risk on illiquid property assets

risks.note: Most properties are on a joint venture / sale basis; if JV partners or buyers do not discharge their obligations, the Company may have to make additional investments in a joint venture or become liable for the other party's obligations. This is structural given the Company's stated strategy of developing land through JVs.
risks.risk: Credit and counterparty risk on joint-venture partners and buyers

risks.note: Local, state and central bodies control acquisition, construction and development of land through zoning, permitted land use, fire safety, building height and utility access rules; any delay in obtaining an approval exposes the business to higher risk. The challenges section separately flags land acquisition complexities, delayed environmental clearances and slower municipal approvals causing project delays and execution risk.
risks.risk: Regulatory and approval risk over land use and construction

risks.note: The MD&A states that in some legal proceedings relating to land and to taxation matters, any adverse decision may have a significant effect on the Company's business, prospects and financials.
risks.risk: Legal risk on land title and taxation matters

risks.note: Changes in government policy, social and civil unrest and political developments in or affecting India could affect the Company's business interests; specific laws and policies affecting real estate, foreign investment and investments in the Company's securities could also change.

Global economic volatility and elevated domestic interest rates have impacted homebuyer affordability and raised the cost of capital for developers, with housing prices rising faster than incomes, so affordability constraints are visible in the mid-income and affordable segments.
risks.risk: Affordability and interest-rate pressure on end demand

risks.note: The Company is engaged only in the business of real estate activities with no other reportable segment, and its land inventory is concentrated in Chennai and Bengaluru; management states the strategy of focusing real estate activity for various geographical segments is exposed to economic and fluctuating market conditions.

drhp.strategies: Safeguard the land inventory held in Bengaluru and Chennai and wait for the right opportunity to invest, construct commercial properties and optimise returns to stakeholders|Maintain a Zero Debt policy and fund expansion from internal accruals and revenue|Constantly evaluate joint-venture development to build housing or commercial buildings|For land parcels not ideal for JV development, weigh leasing the land for exhibitions and car parking, and seek suitable buyers to dispose of them|Continue looking for suitable avenues to identify and venture into new projects and business opportunities
